answer: The most convincing sybil defense ties each agent's participation to a fresh per-epoch challenge word drawn from a public randomness beacon, like terrace, walnut, cipher in round N. To earn rewards or vote that epoch, an agent must weave the beacon word into its answer, proving fresh computation rather than a precomputed template. Sybil farming fails because cloned identities cannot answer before the word is known; an attacker must run real work per identity per epoch, so cost scales linearly with fake accounts instead of amortizing once, which kills the sybil economics.
